claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game requires substantial spending on premium vehicles, premium time, and gold ammo to compete, creating a pay-to-win model.

citations.review_text:
I've played this game since 2012, and seeing how the devs decided to push it into a free-to-play, pay-to-progress model is really sad. I know premium and grind have been there almost since the beginning, but now the game is literally unplayable without buying something. It's basically a subscription-based game hiding behind an F2P mirage.

The game now literally depends on how much cash you're willing to splash, and it has almost nothing to do with skill. You have to pay for premium tanks that are basically tech-tree vehicles but better, or you simply can't compete.
Tier 8, which used to be the most fun tier, is now ruined. Battles are 80% OP premium tanks shooting full gold.
You can't really play the game using standard shells, and if you want to shoot gold, you have to buy premium time and a premium tank, otherwise you'll go broke after three games.
The grind required to get to Tier 10 and 11 is only beaten by Warthunder.

There is literally no balance. The devs just add whatever they feel like and balance it by making it slightly better than the previous tank. This spirals into a strange state where a tank is only considered viable if it is absolutely broken in the hands of a handless monkey.
How can anyone look someone straight in the eyes and say that a Tier 8 premium tank with a 360mm spaced-armour turret is ♥♥♥♥ just because it can't penetrate a Yamato's armour or doesn't have 3,000 DPM?

Around 80% of the tanks in the game are fake, and the vehicle design has gone completely mad. They don't even look like tanks anymore. You have literal race cars with guns, double-barreled IS-3s, and random-ass event box-shaped tanks that are impenetrable by any means.
Before, they at least tried to make the designs look somewhat historical. Now they don't even care about the in-game "history" of the tanks. They just write two paragraphs about how some guy nobody has ever heard of had a thought about an M1A1 Abrams in 1916.

And the tanks that aren't fake often have very lit…

Hell no. And with the Steam installer, even more hell no.
First, the game has turned into a weeny crock of rubbish. Play their way, against unreasonable paywalls, with unreasonable physics and everything tuned to make you pay more and more to stay equal. Basically, unless you want to sink ten years or ten grand into it, you are not "Free to Play", it is definitely "Pay to Win", or if you prefer a more realistic outcome you are treated as "Free to Lose".
And the steam installer stinks. If for any reason you have to reload, the game will reload outside the launcher, and only when it is fully loaded will it then trigger the error "You have to run the game from the Steam launcher". So, a far better experience without Steam altogether.
A classic example of enstuffification by both Wargaming and Valve. The worst possible kind.

Played since the closed beta 15 years ago.  Took a break for 4 or 5 years. Thousands of battles, thousands of hours.  Everything is SO MUCH WORSE lmao.  Everyone just spams gold ammo, even if that ammo is available for silver, wallet warriors have a distinct advantage.  That's not even considering all the premium vehicles.

The UI though.  Holy crap.  Look how they massacred my boy.  It's so cluttered, there are so many stats everywhere, so many different equipment modules to install that all affect your vehicle's stats.  It's all so overwhelming compared to a decade ago.

Also had some REALLY weird encounters in my few PVP matches.  Arty wouldn't have me spotted (made sure to use my crews that were maxed out so I had sixth sense) yet would nail the exact center of my tank multiple times.  Very suspicious.  

Otherwise the majority of the players I encountered would spam premium ammo, you can tell from the bottom left corner of your screen what you were hit with, downright sad.  After just a few battles once I left the warmup games, I uninstalled again.  I miss classic WoT.

Ironically if you want classic WoT, the closest thing you have is WoT on consoles called Modern Armor.  It's less complicated, runs better, and even though it has modern tanks it feels more like WoT than current WoT PC does.  You even only have to worry about one crew, a commander, intead of training a full crew for every tank.  Icing on the cake, a PVE mode you can just relax in.  In WoT PC you only have PVP to grind out your tech tree tanks, which means facing wallet warriors and sweats.

I'll preface this by saying I've played this game for years since I was a kid and have thousands of hours likely.
 I thought I'd try the returning player reward after not playing for over 3 years and saw this on steam. Low and behold my account I hadn't played since before 2022 has been permabanned with no way to make a ticket, I decided to make a ticket on a profile that was connected to the same account for them to close it and say make a ticket on the proper profile if though I can literally access it from the same account. The last battle on said account was in 2023 which I know I hadn't played it since starting my new job so obviously someone else played my account. Still trying to communicate to find out what happened but doubtful they'll help.

  Unless they had made major changes to the game they also suffered from many issues that made it a crap experience. They had "gold ammo" which was prohibitively expensive unless you playing a "premium tank" that players could use with zero downside and increased penetration, they had added premium tanks with no weakspots. It had many of the same issues as war thunder though I would say it was far easier to make money in wot but it has the same game cycle where you load into a game, possibly lose money, and are therefore encouraged to buy a premium account, or buy premium ammo with "paid currency." Or pay money to convert free exp from premium and elite tanks to skip it. Of course with one premium tank you can reasonably deal with these issues but unless you want to dedicate a large portion of your life to this game you won't be making it very far down the tech tree to interesting tanks
They also made some tanks nearly impossible to play without spending free exp to skip the grind on unlocking the better gun for them. The one that comes to mind is the arl v39 french tank destroyer that while being tier 6 starts with a tier 3 gun, meaning you can't pen any half decently armoured tanks in the battles you play.

I've played this game on and off since back when it was in beta (in 2010 or so?). Mostly not on the Steam version, which is why I have practically no playtime listed here. Nevertheless, the Steam version is basically just a more limited version account-wise and plays the exact same as through the original WG launcher, so my comments apply equally here.

The game has had it's ups and downs over the years, but after the 2.0 update in 2025, I have pretty much quit the game. Following the split of the WOWP economy from WOT in 2026, I've basically lost all incentive to even play WOT. I used to play WOWP to farm resources for WOT but eventually, I enjoyed WOWP more than current state WOT and let the resources flow the opposite way (even though it was a trickle compared to the other way around).

It's difficult for me to articulate exactly why I have grown to dislike WOT, but it can basically be summed up as not enjoying the way the game has evolved over time and having no optimism for its future development.
The fact I enjoy WOWP more than WOT when development of WOWP has effectively stalled since before 2020 should reflect my impression of the current state and future trajectory of WOT.

Based on this experience, I cannot honestly suggest that anyone try putting in any amount of time in this game.

citations.review_text: i played this game maybe 15 years ago and i played it again today and its still the same thing... i don't get what is so special about this game... i mean such a huge company and they wont even make a fully destructive environment..

It is very unrealistic for a tank game. The vehicles turn and move far too quickly—something that almost certainly wasn't the case back then. Also, every vehicle has a health bar; this means that even if you fire a massive cannon at a tiny tank, it is highly unlikely to explode. Even though a real-life hit of that caliber would completely destroy the tank, cause it to burst open, or kill the entire crew, the vehicle can simply keep driving, moving, rotating its turret, and reloading just as fast as before. You also cannot fire the machine gun, even though the tanks are equipped with them, which is another very unrealistic aspect. If you are looking for a good tank game, I recommend *War Thunder*. It offers a far superior and more realistic tank gaming experience. Plus, you can use aircraft like dive bombers or ground-attack planes, which makes the experience much better. On top of that, there are far more nations and tanks available, along with a much higher level of realism.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game's monetization as predatory, citing features like loot boxes, paid premium vehicles, and the necessity to spend currency for progression elements such as converting experience or purchasing better ammo.

citations.review_text:
I mainly play from the launcher, hence the low hours count on Steam. All I can say is, this is one of the few games I genuinely pray would meet its downfall soon. I can't remember the last time Wargaming actually showed any care for their game's development, but it must have been back in the 2014-2016 period. 

The current state of the game is nothing but a blatant cash grab. Wargaming has completely lost its direction and added tanks with extremely questionable designs, just to stretch tech trees. If you love, tanks, look away. Wargaming is a company that would do anything to worsen your experience through horrible RNG, finding ways to incentivize you to spend money just to gain an average experience.

It is absolutely ridiculous how monetization works here, from blatant cash grabs being loot boxes to nerfing premium vehicles and making them completely irrelevant, making room for new ones to milk your wallet (I am looking at you, AMX CDC). Oh, and did I mention that apart from buying premium tanks, you have to buy even more gold to convert the EXP earned from them?

I played this game since is came out.
At the start it was a very good arcade shooter, very fun to play with friends, over time is started to go down hill fast, with the introduction of loot boxes, silly made up tanks, playing the same boring stale maps that have only just been reworked, its just stale, the whole monitary system is predatory, for example those tanks with the numbers on them, and the loot boxes at Xmas time, it is just so bad, they pray on people who have no self control on that type of stuff, its poor.

This is one of the worst pay to win games out there.Premium overpowered tanks and loot boxes for sale, unbalanced tech tree tanks, you almost always have to shoot premium ammo because everyone else does and even then the rng is ruthless so if you are a free-to-play player good luck maintaining your credits unless you play premium vehicles .The matchmaking is terrible, even after all these years. It results in games ending in just 3 to 4 minutes, with one team completely obliterating the other with zero effort almost every time.Skill almost never matter if you play in one of those matches because you end up fighting half the enemy team in a matter of minutes because your half team died at the first 3 minutes.Avoid at all costs until these issues are fixed(propably never since they did not cared until now).

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the matchmaking system places newer or lower-tier tanks into matches against significantly higher-tier vehicles and veteran players with thousands of hours.

citations.review_text: I have been playing World of Tanks since 2015, not best player by any means, but I have played for good amount and can say with great sadness that this game is not friendly for new players at all. There is no skill based matchmaking here. People with years upon years of boosters, experience and knowledge will stomp new players, with no way for the new player to know what they did wrong. Last couple of years have been curated for players who are already dedicated hardcore fans, with no major improvements for the new player. I tried to invite a couple of friends along my play time but they only lasted for a month or two at most. I would not recommend the game for someone who is not into this genre in particular.

awful game for new players, dont bother.
its literally first 5 games against bots, then even at tier 2 youre fighing no lives with over 40k games played.
good way to kill the game btw guys.
a 16+ year old game being killed by noobs with over 4k hours who are too bad to play in thier own leauge that instantly tell new players to uninstall the minute they are not running meta equips or do a bad play, its called learning btw.

I'm going to summarize the experience of playing World of Tanks. Basically, it's a bad game. It will drive you nuts. It will make you break your stuff. And it is a very pay-to-win game. Not to mention, you cannot find a match with the same tanks that you're using in your tier. So for example, if you're playing tier 8 or 9, you will end up with tier 10 or even 12 or 13. Not to mention, there is literally no realism to the amount of damage that you put to your enemies. Or even against you. Because if you shoot somebody in, let's say, a weak spot, it will just take away 50 HP. While on the other hand, with one shot from the enemy team, like a random tank, he will take away 200. And I'm not talking about the ammo types because they're all the same. There is no literal meaning for the ammo types. So no, don't play World of Tanks. And if you want a good game to play, just go ahead and play War Thunder. At least that is a realistic experience of tanks and planes and, well, warships. But playing World of Tanks is just hilarious. So yes, go play War Thunder. And I know it is very hard, but at least it's realistic and better than this game that claims to be fun.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the game offers a wide variety of historically grounded vehicles across different classes.

citations.review_text: World of Tanks is an absolute giant of tactical armored warfare that has continually evolved over the years into a deeply refined experience. What I really love about it is the unmatched tactical depth—positioning your hull, carefully managing armor angles, utilizing ridge lines, and exploiting enemy reload windows makes every single engagement feel like a high-stakes chess match. The massive roster of historically grounded vehicles across different classes (from nimble light tanks to powerhouse heavy crushers and stealthy tank destroyers) gives you endless room to match your preferred playstyle.  Recent updates have also done a fantastic job smoothing out quality-of-life features, fine-tuning matchmaking limits, and introducing engaging limited-time modes like Frontline and Last Stand that keep the gameplay fresh. While the steep learning curve, unforgiving mechanics for newcomers, and a heavy endgame grind can test your patience, mastering its core loop is endlessly rewarding. Highly recommend it if you want a deeply strategic, skill-driven multiplayer game

It's a freemium game bordering on pay-to-win, the pricing of premium features is outrageous.

Great variety of vehicles and fun mechanics, game performs well on most machines and the dev team puts an effort into keeping things fresh.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe high-tier progression as heavily reliant on premium accounts, premium ammunition, and paying to avoid severe credit and resource deficits.

citations.review_text:
WoT in 2026 is just as bad as it was in 2020.
100% Pay to Win, if you do not spend money, you will not have any fun.
The entire game is balanced around premium tanks, superior equipment, boosters and premium ammunition.
Do not spend any money on this crap game.

[b]The developers don't want their players to enjoy the product. They want players to suffer and to pay for every drop of positive emotion, and by doing so to build up the player's dependence on spending money.[/b]
 I have been playing this game since 2010 (I am from the beta test) and I have finally moved my account over to Steam in order to leave a review here, so that other people don't waste their time.
[u]Cons :[/u]
- The server list is forever loading, a playable ping is a rare sight, and playing from Canada is hard because of the ping.
- The technical side never gets fixed, yet the economy has been cranked up to the point of absurdity.
- At high tiers there is no point in playing without premium: the grind takes 2-4 times longer, your credits go negative, and you can't consistently play the tank you actually want.
- They added tier 11. On a fair number of tier 10s you can barely scratch their armour, you are just a punching bag.
- Artillery waits 2-3+ minutes for a battle, tanks from tier 7 and up wait 1-2 minutes regardless of the server population, and it rarely drops you in within a couple of seconds.
- There is no balance in team matchmaking, no matter what the developers write. Even battles are rare, usually one of the teams simply falls apart in the first 2-3 minutes.
- In practice the game itself decides when you win or not. You will only get a fair battle after a string of blowouts. It is not you who decides when you win, the game decides it for you by selecting dishonest teams.
- The grind, combined with such poor matchmaking, turns into torture, and at tiers 9-10 the game punishes you with a credit loss even for a win with premium and squeezes you back down to tiers 7-8.
- There are plenty of maps, only a few of them are interesting, and you can't pick them, most maps are built as though the developer had never played the game himself.
- A pile of new maps has been added to the old ones, and on most of them you can't play properly: sit i…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that standard tech tree tanks are heavily outclassed by premium vehicles.

citations.review_text: Played since beta, game just keeps getting worse and worse. Garbage vehicle balancing and matchmaking as well. "Gold" ammo spam is unbearable, makes you question if you are driving a heavily armored steel beast or a plastic toy. The pace of the game has become stupidly fast where some heavy tanks go faster than mediums and matches are over in couple minutes due to poor matchmaking resulting in snowball loss. Armor itself however is  becoming increasingly obsolete with aforementioned gold ammo and introduction of armor flashlight. Consistent spam of premiums by WG that are better than tech tree tanks makes proposition of playing regular tanks pointless especially when you consider how awful stock grinds are. Waste of time, fun game of old is dead. Deleted and good riddance.

DISCLAIMER: I have been playing this game since 2021, i only linked my account to steam this year.

- pay to win 
- most tech tree tanks (free to play & obtain) SUCK to grind until you reach tier 9 
- gold is unbelivably hard to obtain F2P 
- horrendously P2W battlepass that requires gold to unlock "improved pass" 
- bad map design that promotes stale gameplay and punishes proactive movement
- bad playerbase that plays into that issue  
- artillery is unskilled, unfair, and truthfully can be removed without any detriment to the game 
- playing lower tiers is genuinely the only way to enjoy the game anymore in any capacity 
- horrendous lootboxes that cost way too much and give trash rewards 


Feedback: Give players more ways to earn gold & train their tank crews fast, buff all the tech tree tanks until they are up to speed with most premiums, and fix map design by promoting flanking and careful movements. Raise skill floor by removing artillery and the armour penetration indicator feature of showing effective armour (including armour flashlight). Rework gun accuracy system to be dependent on the duration you aim for instead of "leave it up to RNGeezus" so its actually skillful.

World of Tanks is a game I have thousands of hours in, and that makes this review even harder to write...

Because the truth is: I used to love this game. The core concept is still fantastic — tactical tank battles, armor management, positioning, map knowledge, and the satisfaction of mastering a vehicle. Few games have managed to capture the feeling of commanding historical tanks in such an accessible way.

Unfortunately, over the years, many design choices have pushed the game in a direction I can no longer recommend.

The biggest issue is the growing gap between new and experienced players. A newcomer entering the game today has to face years of accumulated content, highly specialized veterans, complex mechanics, and a huge number of powerful premium vehicles. The learning curve has become extremely steep, and the game does very little to make this first experience enjoyable.

The balance has also suffered from years of power creep. Newer tanks, especially premium vehicles, often feel stronger and more forgiving than older ones, making many tech tree vehicles frustrating to play. The increasing importance of premium ammunition also changes the way many engagements play out. What was once a situational tool has become a standard part of high-level gameplay, creating situations where armor and positioning can sometimes feel less meaningful.

The monetization has also become increasingly aggressive. Premium tanks, battle passes, subscriptions, boosters, special events, and various paid systems constantly encourage players to spend money. None of these features are necessarily bad individually, but together they contribute to a feeling that the game is becoming more focused on monetization than on improving the overall experience.

The 2.0 update did bring a welcome breath of fresh air. New content, changes to progression, and some quality-of-life improvements showed that the developers were still trying to evolve the game. For a short time, it felt like World of Tan…
